- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：`os verify` 不再往外部数据源上的对象写测试数据，哪怕该对象开了写入；报告里会写明“外部数据源，未测”。
- 为什么还不能落：README 和 harness 头注释新写的一句说“verify 自己的写都不会到达应用声明的数据源”，但应用若把对象绑到一个声明的 managed 次数据源，verify 仍会写过去（开发自己的报告也这样说）。这句随 npm 包发布就是假话。只需把两处措辞收窄，不改代码。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事，区域修完再送审。

## 席位核对 — REWORK (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `2c3c6e69d38783cda92dd87fcdddd0d40b02a0b7` · 2026-11-19T14:03Z

- **形态** — draft, base `main`, 5 commits, 11 files, +367/−67. Merge-base `5756ae0d`. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35509`: NOT governed, 434 lines ≤ 3000. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; no contract face ⇒ no L2 owed. `Fixes #35255` is right once M1 lands: the seat-ruled shape (leave external objects out, name them "not exercised", no new flag) is built.
- **Must-fix M1 (prose only)** — two sentences this PR writes claim more than the code does:
  - `packages/verify/README.md` (shipped: `files` lists `README.md`): "Datasources the app declares are connected …, so reads of an object bound to one reach that datasource. **Verify's own writes do not**: every derived write family leaves an object on an external datasource out …". The justification covers external datasources only; an object the app binds to a declared datasource with `schemaMode: 'managed'` (or none) is not blocked by `deriveCrudCases` and is written through that datasource, the dev's own second out-of-scope finding (os-dev-report 7011226452).
  - `packages/verify/src/harness.ts` header: "**What verify itself writes stays here**: every derived write family leaves an object on an external datasource out …" — same overclaim.
  - Fix: say what holds, as `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` in this PR already does ("no stage below writes to an object on an external datasource"): verify's own writes never reach an object on an external datasource; an object bound to a declared managed datasource is written through it, as under `os dev`. That keeps the card's "the header and docs match what the test shows". No code or test change needed; L1 delta will read only these lines.
- **Read and holding** (carried to the next head if only M1 moves):
  - `derive.ts`: every object with an `external` block, or on a datasource whose declared `schemaMode` is a string other than `managed`, is `blocked` with `external datasource "NAME" (writes allowed | read-only): not exercised — verify writes only to its ephemeral store`; the gate state only words the reason. The engine's gate (`externalWriteGateClosure`, `engine-registration.ts`) is exactly the `schemaMode` half; the `external`-block half is verify's previous trigger, kept. nit: the changeset attributes both halves to "the way the engine's write gate counts it" — only the first is the engine's.
  - Every write family reads the same case: `rls.ts` (`if (c.blocked) skip`), `reference-shape.ts`, `delete-behavior.ts`, `unique-scope.ts`, `parent-write-reach.ts`, `dashboard-window.ts` all consult `deriveCrudCases(...).blocked` (read at this head).
  - New `verify.external-datasource-no-writes.test.ts`: one boot, a recording driver behind a writable external datasource, CRUD + reference shapes + delete behaviours + unique scopes run; zero writes recorded, each family's report says "not exercised", the CRUD report names the gate open, a requiring managed object skipped and a referencing one verified; CONTROL: a REST create to the same object does reach the driver. The ablation (old `derive.ts`: 10 creates reached the driver) is in the report.
  - Changeset, README and cli.mdx otherwise read sentence by sentence: the seed/hook/flow sentence and the `--flow` confinement sentence match the code and the ruled shape.
- **Your question 1 — the four files outside the claimed surface: accepted.** `option-b-reader-probe.ts` row B2 and `artifact-collections.test.ts` are cross-package witnesses of `deriveCrudCases`'s datasource map that asserted an *unblocked* write-opted-in external case; this PR makes that assertion false by design, so they had to move, and each now reads the map through the reason's `(writes allowed)`, which still fails a reader that resolves `objects` but not `datasources`. The other two edits are comments that would otherwise describe the old gate. They are tests of `derive.ts` (the claim's "their tests"), named in the dev's deviations; not an adjacent-defect widening.
- **Your question 2 — the non-managed `schemaMode` arm: inside the card's shape.** The card is "an object on an external datasource"; a datasource is external, by the engine's own write gate, exactly when its declared `schemaMode` is not `managed`. Without this arm an object bound to such a datasource by `schemaMode` alone (no `external` block) would still be written, which the card forbids.
- **Your question 3 — the three out-of-scope findings:**
  - (b) **managed secondary datasource still written: card owed**, p2 like this card (test rows can reach a real database behind a declared datasource; reach not measured), `area:build`, citing os-dev-report 7011226452 and this record. It is the half of the card's "Expected: the CRUD phase writes only to the ephemeral stack" this ruled shape does not cover. Dedupe words as the dev gave them.
  - (a) app seed / hook / flow writes still reach a writable external datasource: **no card owed from L1.** It is the alternative shape (confine every write, as `--flow` does) the seat ruled against for this card, and after M1 the README, header, docs and changeset all state it. Re-opening it is the seat's call.
  - (c) cascade message generic for a managed object requiring an external one: **wording nit, no card of its own** — fold it into (b)'s card as a line item.
